pageCache.pageTitle: Elevated Futures Education – A Strength-Based Ethos
pageCache.text:
Learning Spaces
I used to hate school. Not anymore.
To be honest, before I came to Elevated Futures, I thought school just wasn’t for me.
At my old school, it felt like I was always in trouble or just “the child who couldn’t keep up.” Every meeting, every conversation with teachers, was just a list of what I was doing wrong, what I was “bad at,” or how I was “failing to meet expectations.” I felt like I was a problem that needed to be fixed, and after a while, I just stopped trying.
The first week at Elevated Futures was weird. In my first conversation, they didn’t start with a list of my problems. The first thing they asked me was, “What are you good at?”
I didn’t know how to answer. No one had ever really asked me that before.
But we talked, and my teachers here helped me see that the things my old school called “distractions” were actually my strengths. They told me I had a “superpower” for logic and creative design (I love building complex worlds in games).
That’s what the Dynamic Development Plan (DDP) is. It’s not like my old, dusty IEP. My DDP is my plan. I’m actually in the meetings, and I help write my own goals.
And it’s not just about grades; it’s about everything. When I get overwhelmed or angry, it’s not an instant detention. My DDP has a goal for it. We talk about why I’m overwhelmed, and my teachers help me learn the skills to handle it. They understand that my behaviour is just me communicating that I’m struggling.
It’s the first time I’ve ever felt like my teachers are on my team.
I’m not “managing my problems” here. I’m using my “superpower” to help me with the stuff I find hard. For my Enterprise project, I’m using my design skills to build a 3D model, and it’s actually counting towards my accreditation.
I’m not just “a problem” at this school. I’m just me. And for the first time, that feels like it’s more than
Join Our Purpose-Led Team
Professional Opportunities in Southwark
At Elevated Futures Education, we are expanding our specialised team of educators and support professionals on our Southwark campus. As an independent school provision currently awaiting our final registration confirmation letter, we are actively seeking passionate practitioners who align with our strengths-based philosophy. If you are committed to the principles of our Dynamic Development Plan and wish to support young people within a neuro-affirming environment, we invite you to explore our current career opportunities.
We offer a unique, collaborative workspace within the vibrant London South Bank University footprint, where professional growth and staff wellbeing are deeply valued. Discover how your expertise can help us awaken potential and redefine the landscape of Special Educational Needs.
Why Choose Our School?
A choice that makes the difference. for your child
A DDP-Led, Strengths-Based Model
A Genuinely Holistic & Therapeutic Team
Building Confidence & Self-Advocacy for Life
Welcome to Elevated Futures Education
Welcome to Elevated Futures, a specialist provision where we believe that discovering and becoming the best version of ourselves is a joyous process. We have a strong academic focus, but we are equally passionate about education in the broadest possible sense.
Our entire culture is built on the Dynamic Development Plan (DDP), a strengths-based philosophy that ensures every student's unique "superpower" is the key to their success. With an impressive array of co-curricular activities, from our partnership with Shakespeare's Globe Theatre to our in-house therapeutic support, we create a community where everyone belongs and is empowered to develop their own sense of self.

pageCache.text:
Welcome to Elevated Futures
Elevated Futures is the realisation of a career dedicated to championing strengths-based learning. Doreen Sinclair-McCollin, B.Ed (Hons), NPQH, NLP Diploma, is a qualified and experienced education leader, behaviour consultant, life coach, and advocate for children and parents.
As Founder and CEO of Elevated Minds CIC, Doreen has spent over 38 years working with young people and families, both in mainstream and alternative provision settings.
Under her leadership, this provision has been shaped to embody the DDP philosophy, drawing on Doreen’s deeply held conviction that every young person, regardless of background or prior challenge, can flourish when their strengths are recognised, nourished and given the opportunity to shine.
Driven by her own early experience of education exclusion in her family, she is committed to closing the gap between potential and performance, creating educational spaces where young people thrive with confidence, autonomy and purpose.
Her leadership style is marked by vision, compassion and unwavering determination to ensure that Elevated Futures is not simply a school but a transformative community, one that empowers young people, supports families, and changes lives.
Our Philosophy in Action
The DDP model is designed to create accelerated progress by changing the entire approach to pupil support.
The moment we stop focusing on deficits and identify the pupil's strengths.
Stagnant Progress
Fixed IEP Targets
Low Engagement
Behaviour Incidents
Accelerated Progress
Holistic Goals Met
Builds Self-Advocacy
Successful Post-16 Transition
The "Elevation Arc" Explained
The diagram above is more than a graphic; it is the visual representation of our "why."
The "Old Path" (the flat, grey line) represents the journey of a pupil in a traditional, deficit-based system. Their progress is often stagnant, defined by a fixed IEP, low engagement, and a focus on "managing behaviour."
The "DDP Intervention" (the gold circle) is the catalyst for change. This is the moment we stop, listen, and, through our "Strengths-Finding" process, identify that pupil's unique "superpower." We shift the focus from "what's wrong" to "what are you great at?"
The "Elevation Arc" (the accelerating teal curve) is the result. By leveraging that "superpower" as the gateway to the curriculum, we create a new, upward path. Progress becomes dynamic, holistic goals are met, and pupils build the self-advocacy and confidence they need. This is how we achieve our mission: by elevating the future of every pupil.
See How We Do It
Our philosophy is built into the fabric of our school.

pageCache.text:
Reimagining Education: From Static Institutions to Dynamic Futures
For over a century, our language for education has been institutional: schools, colleges, academies. These terms evoke a specific, industrial-era model—a physical building, a fixed timetable, age-based cohorts, and a "one-size-fits-all" curriculum. But what happens when this model is no longer fit for purpose, especially for young people who think differently?
The term "Education Futures" suggests a new vision. It is not just a place, but a provision; not an institution, but a hub. It is a fundamental shift in philosophy, moving from a static system of knowledge transfer to a dynamic, holistic learning environment designed to build the skills for a rapidly changing world.
The Deficit of the Institutional Model
Traditional institutions are often built on a "deficit" model. They measure pupils against a fixed standard, and those who do not fit are labelled as having "problems" to be "managed." Their journey is defined by what they cannot do.
An "Education Future," by contrast, is a specialist setting built on a "strengths-based" model. It rejects the institutional conveyor belt. It understands that the goal is not to force a pupil to fit the system, but to design a system that fits the pupil.
The Core of the New Model: A DDP-Led Provision
A true "Education Future" provision is defined by its agility. It is a collaborative hub where teachers, therapists, parents, and pupils work together around a central, living document—a Dynamic Development Plan (DDP).

In this model, we are not building another school. We are building a Centre of Excellence, a specialist provision that acts as a blueprint for the future of education: one that is dynamic, strengths-based, and, above all, successful in its mission to elevate the futures of all young people.

pageCache.text:
Our Curriculum Intent
Our curriculum is unashamedly ambitious for every pupil. Its primary intent is to provide a deeply personalised, strengths-based, and holistic education that empowers pupils to discover their superpowers, achieve ambitious academic and personal outcomes, and transition into a successful and independent adult life.
We reject a deficit-based model of education. Instead, our curriculum is built upon the Dynamic Development Plan (DDP), a framework that leverages pupil strengths to unlock access to learning and overcome challenges.
Our Aims
Deliver the National Curriculum
Championing Strengths
Develop the Whole Site
Create Independent Futures
Use Our Community
The DDP Golden Thread: Our Implementation
We implement our curriculum intent through a cohesive five-year journey, with the DDP as the golden thread connecting all learning.
The DDP Journey: From Discovery to Independence
KS3 (Discovery & Identity)
The DDP is a living document co-created with the pupil and family. It is a tool for self-discovery, identifying strengths, and setting personal goals (academic, social, and emotional).
KS4 (Strategic Action)
The DDP evolves into a strategic action plan. It is the central document for careers guidance, post-16 planning, and managing the pressures of accreditation, giving pupils ownership of their transition.
How We Teach
Our curriculum is delivered through a blend of core subjects, cross-curricular projects, and integrated therapeutic support. All planning starts with the pupil's DDP.
This approach allows us to be flexible and responsive, ensuring that every pupil can access the full curriculum in a way that is meaningful to them.
This core project runs from Y7 to Y11. In KS3, it focuses on identity, strengths, and community. In KS4, it evolves to deliver all Gatsby Benchmarks, managing work experience, CV writing, and post-16 applications.
The National Curriculum is delivered through DDP-led planning. A pupil's superpower in creative writing is used as the gateway to analytical texts. Maths is relentlessly practical, linked to the Enterprise and Financial Literacy strands. Science is hands-on, leveraging pupil curiosity.
These are not soft subjects; they are core to our DDP model. They provide a primary vehicle for non-verbal expression, managing challenging emotions, and building a tangible portfolio of skills (e.g., Arts Award, Sports Leaders, IT qualifications).
Learning Without Walls - The 3 L's
Financial Literacy
A five-year plan from "Wants vs. Needs" in Y7 to "Budgeting for Independence" in Y11, all linked to our Maths and Enterprise projects.
Digital Literacy & Online Safety
Explicitly teaching pupils about online safety, AI, misinformation, and digital wellbeing to meet KCSIE guidelines.
Environmental Literacy
Empowering pupils to understand their impact on the world through sustainability projects, conservation awareness, and hands-on environmental stewardship.
Leveraging Our Local Community
Southwark as a Classroom
We use our local assets to build cultural capital, including partnerships with Shakespeare's Globe, Tate Modern, and local businesses, making our surrounding borough an extension of the school.
Teacher Handbook
A print-ready guide for staff on how to use the DDP curriculum, frameworks, medium-term plans and assessment resources consistently across the school.
Open the Teacher Handbook (PDF)
Use this handbook to support planning, delivery, evidence capture, assessment, quality assurance and staff consistency across the full DDP curriculum suite.
Our Impact: The Elevation Arc
We measure the success of our curriculum by the tangible, long-term outcomes for our pupils.
How We Measure Success (Our Proof)
Ready to See the Difference?
Explore our assessment policies in detail or get in touch with our admissions team.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Courses – Elevated Futures EducationProfessional Development Catalogue | Elevated Futures Education
pageCache.text:
Awakening the Workforce
2026/27 Training Suite
1. Diagnostic & Profiling Practice
Cognitive Asset Profiler Certification
This intensive certification trains staff to conduct robust, forensic screenings for neurodivergent traits. We move away from deficit-based labeling and focus on the cognitive, sensory, and emotional assets that a student brings.
The Neuro-Attunement Coach
Training support staff in the art of relational co-regulation. Learn to monitor the physiological state of a learner in real-time, delivering reset interventions that protect the safe base.
2. Leadership & Strategy
The Architect of Inclusion
A strategic leadership programme for SENCOs who want to redesign their provision, focusing on forensic EHCP management and adaptive teaching models.
Designing for Awakening
For Curriculum Leads. Learn how to sequence content using the Oak National Academy or your own curriculum framework while weaving the "Golden Thread" of DDP philosophy.
Navigating Statutory Change
Unpicking SEND reforms. Strategic tools to implement government policy without sacrificing the restorative, clinical integrity of your school.
3. Pedagogy & Regulation
Beyond Adaptation: Masterclass in Neuro-Attunement
Transformative training for classroom teachers. Shift practice from simple environmental changes to deep, relational attunement and the building of classroom sanctuaries.
De-escalation to Attunement
Interpret dysregulation as a communication of need. Learn to respond with regulatory interventions that keep the student engaged in the Elevation Arc.
4. Student Leadership & Foundational Awareness
Neuromentor Leadership Certification
Empowers students to become trained "Lived Experience Leaders." Participants become peer mentors, offering relational attunement and regulatory resets to their peers.
Foundations of the Sanctuary
Essential entry-level course for new staff. Introduces the DDP, the Elevation Arc, and the language of unconditional appreciation. The "day one" mandate for every practitioner.

pageCache.text:
Know Your Rights, Secure the Right Placement
A parent's guide to requesting that Elevated Futures Education is named on your child's EHCP.
EHCP School Placement Guide
If your child has, or is applying for, an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP), you have a legal right to ask the Local Authority (LA) to name a particular school in it, including Elevated Futures Education. This guide explains that right in plain English, what it means for you and your child, and gives you a sample letter to get started.
This page is general information, not legal advice. Every EHCP is different, so if you are unsure of your own situation, see the "Where to get further help" section below.
What the law actually says
Under Section 38(3) of the Children and Families Act 2014, when the LA sends you a draft EHCP (or a draft amended plan at an annual review), you can request that a specific school, academy, college or approved independent/non-maintained special school is named in Section I of the plan.
Once you make that request, under Section 39(4) the LA must name the school unless at least one of these applies:
This is sometimes called a "qualified duty", it isn't absolute, but the bar for the LA to refuse is genuinely high, and they must be able to evidence it.
Rights at a Glance
An EHCP sets out rights for both you as a parent or carer, and for your child directly.
Parents & Carers Can
Name a preferred school when the draft plan is issued, request an early annual review, appeal a refusal to the SEND Tribunal, and be consulted at every stage of the process.
Your Child's Rights
The EHCP is an entitlement that belongs to your child, not an obligation on you. Their views, wishes and feelings must be actively sought and recorded, and the named school must be funded and provision delivered in full.
If the LA Refuses
The LA must give clear, evidenced reasons under Section 39(4). You can challenge this through mediation or by appealing to the First-tier Tribunal (SEND).
Timing Matters
You don't have to wait for the annual review, you can request a school is named whenever a draft or draft amended plan is issued, including at an early review.
How to Request Elevated Futures Education Is Named
A straightforward, step-by-step route through the process.
1. Wait for your draft plan
The right to name a school applies when the LA sends you a draft EHCP, or a draft amended plan following a review.
2. Put your request in writing
Write to the caseworker named on the plan, stating clearly which school you want named in Section I. Use the sample letter below as a starting point.
3. Ask us to help with evidence
Contact our office, we can provide information about how we can meet your child's needs, and confirm we have (or can offer) a place, which supports the LA's consultation.
4. Give reasons linked to your child's needs
Explain, where you can, why this school is right for your child, referencing their needs in Sections B and F of the plan, not just a general preference.
5. Keep to the timescale
Respond within the timeframe given on the draft plan (usually 15 calendar days) so your request is considered as part of that draft.
6. If refused, ask why, then consider your options
Any refusal must set out which Section 39(4) reason applies. You can request mediation, or appeal to the SEND Tribunal within two months of the final plan.
Sample Letter: Requesting a Named School
Adapt this template to your own circumstances and your child's needs before sending it.
[Your name] [Your address] [Date]
[SEN Caseworker name] [Local Authority SEND Team] [LA address]
Re: [Child's full name], DOB [date of birth], EHCP reference [reference number if known]
Dear [Caseworker name],
I am writing further to the draft Education, Health and Care Plan for [child's name], received on [date]. Under Section 38(3) of the Children and Families Act 2014, I am requesting that Elevated Futures Education is named as the school in Section I of [child's name]'s EHCP.
I believe Elevated Futures Education is able to meet [child's name]'s needs as set out in Sections B and F of the draft plan, in particular [briefly note relevant needs/provision, e.g. "their need for a highly structured, individualised curriculum delivered through the Dynamic Development Plan approach"]. [Optionally add: I understand the school has confirmed it can offer a place / I have visited the school and believe it is suitable, because...]
Under Section 39(4) of the Act, I understand the Local Authority must name this school unless it is unsuitable for [child's name]'s age, ability, aptitude or needs, or would be incompatible with the efficient education of others or the efficient use of resources. I do not believe either exception applies here, and would welcome the opportunity to discuss this further if the Local Authority disagrees.
Please could you confirm receipt of this request and let me know the next steps and timescales. I look forward to hearing from you within the statutory timeframe.
Yours sincerely, [Your name] [Contact telephone number] [Email address]
Where to Get Further Help
These independent, free services specialise in EHCP and SEND rights and can support you further:
Our team is also always happy to talk this through with you, see Key Contacts to get in touch.
Know Your Rights: SEND Code of Practice
Seven key points from the SEND Code of Practice and the Children and Families Act 2014, at a glance.
A Named School Is a Legal Commitment
Once a school is written into Section I of an EHCP, the Local Authority must secure that placement. This is not a preference on paper, it is a statutory duty.
Your Child Has the Right to Attend Now
Once a plan is finalised, provision should begin without unnecessary delay, not "once funding is sorted" or once administrative processes catch up.
Funding Is Not a Legal Reason for Delay
Local Authorities cannot lawfully delay a placement or provision while internal budgets, panels or funding processes are resolved. Your child's education comes first.
The Local Authority Must Secure the Placement
Arranging the agreed school place is the LA's statutory duty under the Children and Families Act 2014. This duty is enforceable in law.
Your Child's EHCP Is Enforceable
Section F sets out the specific provision your child is entitled to. If it is written into the plan, it must be delivered in full, not partially, and not "when possible".
Delays Breach the Children and Families Act
The law requires timely action at every stage of the EHCP process. Unreasonable administrative delay is unlawful, not simply inconvenient.
Parents Are Equal Partners in SEND Decisions
Your views carry legal weight throughout the process. You are not a passenger in your child's EHCP, you are a decision-maker.

pageCache.text:
Our Commitment to Safeguarding
Elevated Futures is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of all children. We believe every child has the right to feel safe, valued, and respected. We are alert to the signs of abuse and neglect and follow clear procedures to ensure children receive effective support, protection, and justice.
Our provision offers a trauma-informed and neuro-affirming environment, with particular attention to the needs and vulnerabilities of autistic and ADHD learners. We recognise the close links between safeguarding and mental health and are committed to early identification, support, and appropriate intervention.
Safeguarding is embedded throughout our curriculum, pastoral work, coaching model, and wider culture. We promote respectful relationships and challenge any form of prejudice, discrimination, or harmful attitudes that could place children at risk.
Our Safeguarding Team
If you have any concerns about the safety or welfare of a child, please contact one of our Designated Safeguarding Leads (DSLs) immediately.
Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL)
Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead
Doreen Sinclair-McCollin
What to do if you have a concern:
Report it immediately to a DSL.
Do not investigate it yourself.
Do not promise confidentiality.
Online Safety & Emerging Risks
We are explicitly committed to meeting all KCSIE 2025 guidelines. Our curriculum provides specific education on new and emerging online threats.
External Help & Our Full Policy
You can find links to our external safeguarding partners and our full, detailed policy documents below.
Southwark MASH
If you have a concern about a child, you can contact the Multi-Agency Safeguarding Hub.
LADO / Ofsted
If you have a concern about an adult working with children, contact the LADO on 020 7525 0689.
Ofsted: 0300 123 4666
Read Our Full Policy
Our complete, KCSIE-aligned policy details all our procedures, including Prevent, recruitment, and record keeping.

Our Assessment Procedures
At Elevated Futures, assessment is a tool for understanding, not just measuring. We have moved beyond deficit, based models that simply identify gaps. Our assessment procedures are designed to discover, celebrate, and build upon pupil strengths.
Our Core Principles:
The Elevation Arc in Action
Our curriculum is designed to move learners from the clinical sanctuary of our provision toward the academic autonomy of higher education. This visualisation represents the journey toward mastery, where every student is empowered to reach their next educational milestone.
Statutory Policy Library
Here you can find our full library of statutory policies, procedures, and key documents. All our policies are DDP, informed and reviewed annually by the proprietor.
Pupil Premium Strategy
Our innovation, led roadmap for sustaining learner achievement and sovereignty.
Accessibility Plan
Our three, year strategic plan for improving access to learning and facilities.
Anti, Bullying Policy
Fostering a safe and supportive community built on mutual respect.
Attendance Policy
Our DDP-led, support-first approach to helping every pupil attend and thrive.
Behaviour Policy
Our therapeutic, skills, based approach to self, regulation and relationships.
Complaints Policy
Our formal procedure for parents, carers, and community stakeholders.
Curriculum Policy
The core philosophy and framework driving our academic and clinical provision.
Curriculum Intent
Our strategic framework for neuro, affirming pedagogy and learner awakening.
Curriculum Plan
The detailed five, year thematic curriculum overview and schemes of work.
Health and Safety
Mandatory procedures for ensuring a safe clinical sanctuary for all.
Mobile Phone Policy
How we keep our school mobile phone-free, calm and safe for every learner.
Physical Intervention Policy
Our approach to preventing and reducing restrictive interventions, and to searching.
Assessment Procedures
Our DDP, led policy on diagnostic tracking and academic reporting.
Safeguarding Policy
Our KCSIE, aligned child protection policy and restorative safety protocols.
Safer Recruitment Policy
How we recruit safely, so every adult working with our pupils is suitable.
Equality & Diversity
Our institutional commitment to equal opportunities and inclusion.
SEND Policy
How we identify, celebrate, and support neurodivergent learning profiles.
Have a Question?
If you have any questions about our policies, please get in touch.
The Sovereignty Pathway
Innovation in Sustained Achievement
Our Pupil Premium Strategy is a clinical roadmap for restorative progress, ensuring that every learner moves from the clinical sanctuary of our provision toward the academic autonomy of higher education. We prioritise the development of metacognitive agency, teaching our young people to become the primary citizens of their own success.
By utilising the borough of Southwark as our laboratory, we bridge the gap between classroom theory and real, world application. This visualisation represents our commitment to the Elevation Arc, where academic rigour and neuro, affirming practice converge to create lasting, life, changing outcomes at institutions like LSBU.

Statutory Registration Status
Ofsted Pre-Registration & Readiness
The Pre-Registration Inspection Process
The pre-registration inspection is a statutory requirement for all proposed independent schools in the United Kingdom, serving as the definitive process through which the Department for Education and Ofsted verify that a new provision has the capacity to meet the rigorous Education Regulations. This process evaluates our proposed arrangements for safeguarding, the suitability of the proprietor, the quality of curriculum delivery, and the physical safety of the premises.
For Elevated Futures Education, this assessment represents the verification of our clinical and educational model. It ensures that our environment is prepared to function as a therapeutic sanctuary where the curriculum is accessible and every interaction is restorative.
Our Successful Readiness Report
Our successful pre-registration readiness report is the vital statutory instrument that allows Elevated Futures Education to be formally registered as an operating school. The inspectors reviewed our comprehensive schemes of work, our staffing structures, and our specialized tracking tools. The report confirms that our provision meets all the necessary standards, validating our capacity to offer an outstanding educational experience.
The outcomes of this inspection prove that our pioneering Dynamic Development Plan is fully compliant with the regulatory expectations of the DfE. This successful assessment gives local authorities and families absolute confidence in our ability to deliver a safe, structured, and highly effective environment for neurodivergent young people.
Note: The official report will open in a secure new browser window.
